title: Under the Point
passages:
They went out through the gap where the door had swollen shut, Kornél first with the ledger against his chest, Ruzsa behind with the tarp over her head, Ákos last with Sára’s living hand knotted in his coat. The water was knee-deep and moving fast, pulling at their legs. The hut groaned behind them and settled. No one looked back.

Kornél stopped at the top of the sunken path. The ledger’s ink line ran from the page’s edge toward a drowned fence, then bent left, under the water. “Pilot’s mark,” he said. “The channel goes under the Point. We don’t cross the river. We go down it.” Ruzsa laughed once, without humor. “Under the Point is where the toll house keeps its dead.” Ákos held the notebook above the water. “Then that’s where Ilka’s name went.”

Sára’s dead hand rose from her side and pointed at the black water. Her living hand tightened on Ákos’s coat until he felt the seam give. He did not pull away. Kornél tied the cord to a post, tested it, and stepped down. The water took him to the waist. The cord went slack, then drew a short, hard line toward the left. He followed it. Ruzsa swore and followed. Ákos went after, Sára’s grip dragging at his coat, the ledger’s ink line bright under the rain.

At the bottom of the steps, the water was still. A stone shelf ran under the Point, dry except for a film of river. The ledger’s line ended at a crack in the stone. From the crack came a sound like a bell struck once, far off. Sára’s mouth shaped *Ilka*. The fourteenth mark on the page darkened, and a fifteenth began to form, thin as a hair.

The fifteenth mark quivered on the page, a thin black hair lifting from the paper. The bell answered from the crack, one note that ran down the ledger’s ink line and into the stone. Kornél’s cord drew tight; he made a low sound in his throat and braced his heel. Ruzsa’s tarp whispered. Ákos held the notebook steady, but Sára’s living hand gripped his coat so hard the seam split.

Sára’s dead hand came up from her side. It was ink-stained and slow, lifting toward the ledger as if it had a life of its own. Kornél said, “Don’t let it write.” Sára’s mouth shaped *Ilka* again, and her dead hand pressed the ledger’s edge. The ink line from the page curled down the stone shelf and touched the crack. The bell rang under the stone, not through it. The crack opened along a ridge, smooth as a spine, and the ledger seemed to lean into it.

Ruzsa stepped forward. “I’ll give the next mark,” she said. Her voice was steady, which scared them more than fear. “The White Water knowledge. For the fifteenth. I’ll pay it.” Ákos looked at the notebook, then at the ledger. Kornél pulled the cord taut, and the slack drew tight. The fifteenth mark brightened, waiting.

Sára’s dead hand cut the ink line. The ledger made no sound, but the bell stopped. The fifteenth mark stayed thin, then faded. The crack closed with a sound like a spine settling. Ruzsa kept her hand over the notebook, and the page grew warm under her palm.

Ruzsa kept her hand over the notebook, and the page grew warm under her palm. The ink on the ledger’s edge shivered, a thin line of black crawling up the stone shelf toward the crack that had just sealed itself. The warm page pulsed as if breathing, and a faint scent of river mud rose from the paper. A new tally mark formed, thin as a hair, just beyond the faded fifteenth, and the word *River* appeared in the margin, its letters dark against the paper.

Ákos felt the split in his coat widen, the seam tearing further as Sára’s living hand squeezed tighter, pulling at his shoulder. Sára’s dead hand lifted, its ink‑stained fingers hovering over the fresh mark, then dropped onto the ledger’s edge. Kornél’s cord snapped taut, humming as the ledger called, and he stepped forward, eyes fixed on the new tally. Ruzsa lifted her hand, the notebook now cool, and whispered, “Take what you need.” The ledger’s ink surged, filling the empty space with the word *River* before fading, leaving the page heavy with memory.

The group stood in the dripping silence, the ledger’s spine now a closed crack, but the new mark lingered, waiting for the next hand. The cord remained tight, the bell’s echo faded, and the water around the shelf glistened, reflecting the faint glow of the ink. With the word *River* recorded, the ledger seemed to acknowledge Ruzsa’s offer, yet the next tally remained unfilled, urging the travelers to decide their next move.
